sources.title: The People's Republic of China Third National Communication on Climate Change
sources.organization: People's Republic of China; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Government-approved communication dated December 2018; observed climate and sector trends and future scenarios, generally updated through 2015.
sources.methodology: Government-approved UNFCCC report combining observed trends and modeled risks.
sources.limitations: Unofficial translation; underlying studies are dated and projections are not measurements.

sources.title: Progress Report on China's Climate Change Adaptation (2024) / 中国适应气候变化进展报告（2024）
sources.organization: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
sources.temporal_coverage: Official 33-page review of climate conditions and adaptation activities in 2024; includes implementation status through February 2025.
sources.methodology: Ministry report reviewing national climate observations, sector actions and regional adaptation measures.
sources.limitations: Government progress account; program coverage and reported outputs are not independent outcome evaluations.

sources.title: 2024 national situation of natural disasters
sources.organization: National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief Office and Ministry of Emergency Management of China
sources.temporal_coverage: Calendar-year 2024 disaster impacts reported by local emergency-management departments and reviewed by national agencies.
sources.methodology: Annual bulletin compiled from local emergency reports and inter-agency review; includes hazard-specific and regional totals.
sources.limitations: Administrative impact estimates; the bulletin does not attribute individual disasters to climate change.

sources.title: MEM publishes typical cases of successful disaster avoidance in 2024 / 应急管理部公布2024年度全国成功避险避灾典型案例
sources.organization: Ministry of Emergency Management of China
sources.temporal_coverage: National ministry's selected 2024 disaster-avoidance cases, published 6 June 2025.
sources.methodology: Ministry-selected case reports drawn from local submissions and expert review of 437 reported cases.
sources.limitations: Selected successful cases illustrate response processes, not representative rates or independently evaluated impact.

claims.paraphrase: The communication identifies the Loess Plateau as China's most agriculturally vulnerable area; observed yield reductions affected one crop type on 90% and two types on 55% of its arable land.
claims.limitations: Cites underlying study; no household disaggregation.

claims.paraphrase: Warming and drying reduced northern-grassland forage yield and capacity, most in central-eastern Inner Mongolia and southeastern Gansu.
claims.limitations: Ecological indicator; no measured household livelihood effect.

claims.paraphrase: By mid-century, water vulnerability is projected to intensify in Haihe, Yellow, Huaihe and Song-Liao basins under combined climate change and rising demand.
claims.scenario: Medium greenhouse-gas concentration scenario; comparison period 2021–2050 versus 1961–1990.

claims.paraphrase: The report projects less snow and greater cryosphere vulnerability in Tibet, including great or extreme levels in some areas.
claims.scenario: Future climate projections; the cited passage does not specify a single time horizon or emissions pathway.

claims.paraphrase: MEE reports 2024 national precipitation 9% above the 1991–2020 norm; Yangtze-Huaihe Meiyu rainfall exceeded normal by over 50%, and North China rainy-season precipitation by 83%.
claims.limitations: Annual aggregate and regional rainfall anomalies; not an event-attribution study.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 10–11, integrated disaster prevention and early action
claims.paraphrase: In 2024, China added 9,944 geological-hazard warning stations; six administrative levels logged 600,000 risk reports and helped move over 10,000 households and 30,000 people before danger.
geographies: provincial, county, township and village levels
institutions: National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief
claims.limitations: Government-reported outputs; no independent assessment of warning coverage or evacuation outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: MEE identifies the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau as a key vulnerable region, reporting cross-ministry coordination and research; along the Yellow River, 333.8 hectares of riverside greening were added in 2024.
claims.limitations: Coordination and greening are reported activities, not evaluated resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 21 and MEE publication summary, provincial plans and climate-adaptive city pilots
claims.paraphrase: By February 2025, 30 provinces and Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps had adaptation plans; 39 cities were climate-adaptive pilots, alongside a 2025–2027 early-warning action plan.
claims.limitations: Plan and pilot counts do not measure implementation quality or reduced losses.

claims.paraphrase: Local emergency departments reported 94.13 million person-times affected by disasters in 2024, 856 deaths or missing, and 3.645 million emergency relocations nationwide.
claims.limitations: Reported person-times are not necessarily unique individuals; annual totals combine hazards.

claims.locator: HTML paragraph 56, 2024 flood and geological-disaster impacts
claims.paraphrase: Floods and geological disasters affected 53.449 million person-times and displaced 2.544 million; July events in Shangluo/Baoji, Shaanxi, and Chenzhou/Hengyang, Hunan, caused 95 and 94 deaths or missing, respectively.
claims.limitations: Annual report gives event impacts but does not attribute these events to climate change.

claims.paraphrase: Super Typhoon Yagi affected Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi and Yunnan in September 2024, causing four deaths and 189,000 collapsed or damaged houses, with reported direct losses of 72.03 billion yuan.
claims.limitations: Official aggregate impact figures; no local distribution or climate attribution given.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 91–94, Qinglong County landslide case
claims.paraphrase: In Tunshang Village, Zima Township, Qinglong County, Guizhou, warning and joint inspections led to 180 people moving from a landslide-risk area; 53 houses were damaged, with no deaths.
claims.limitations: Ministry-selected successful case; the report does not provide a counterfactual.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 104–107, Hubei flood and levee-seepage case
claims.paraphrase: In Yangjiawan Village, Huangzhou District, Hubei, local reporters spotted levee seepage; a 150-person, 18-machine response controlled it, averting flood exposure for 240,000 people and 320,000 mu of farmland.
claims.limitations: Case reports estimated people and land protected, not observed avoided losses.

claims.locator: HTML paragraphs 166–169, Beijing Pinggu District evacuation case
claims.paraphrase: Before August 2024 storms, Pinggu District responders checked households including older, infirm, disabled and non-local residents in Tawa Village; 257 people were relocated from flood and landslide risk.
institutions: Pinggu District Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters
claims.limitations: Selected successful case; no disaggregated outcome evaluation.

search_audit.query: China official climate vulnerability subnational reports water agriculture plateau grassland crop yields disaster 2024
search_audit.outcome: Opened the UNFCCC national communication and MEE 2024 adaptation report plus national and local disaster records; found named basins, ecoregions and event locations, but little household-level disaggregation.

search_audit.query: China climate change conflict violence resource competition official government UN report
search_audit.outcome: Search and full-text review found climate, livelihood and disaster vulnerabilities but no China-specific primary evidence connecting them to armed or political violence; no such pathway is asserted.

search_audit.query: China insecurity conflict violence disruption climate adaptation disaster response official report
search_audit.outcome: The inspected adaptation and disaster sources report planning, warning and response activity, but no conflict or insecurity disrupting climate action; search did not locate country-specific primary evidence of this reverse pathway.

search_audit.query: China climate adaptation resilience capacity official early warning provincial plan local evacuation case report
search_audit.outcome: MEE documents adaptation plans, regional coordination and warning systems; MEM case reports show named village-level monitoring, inter-agency response and evacuation for exposed residents.

gaps: CHN is not listed in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json, and no countries/CHN baseline directory exists in this worktree; this extraction therefore has no pre-existing China dossier to extend.

No inspected China-specific primary source explicitly links climate hazards to FCV violence or conflict, or conflict insecurity to adaptation interruption; these links remain unsubstantiated rather than assumed absent.

The most geographically detailed national climate vulnerability assessment is the 2018 Third National Communication, an unofficial English translation using dated underlying studies; projected risks should not be read as current measurements.

National disaster totals and selected successful-response cases are government-reported; climate attribution, household-level vulnerability for most locations and independent outcome evaluation were not available in the inspected sources.
